$comment: COPY → ~/.paseo-pi-team/cluster-routing.local.json on the CONTROLLER host. Never commit the local copy. This is the single controller-local route file: every host in the cluster is described here, each with its own connection, capabilities, concurrency limits and per-class routes. Endpoint VALUES (pairing offers / remote targets) live ONLY in environment variables referenced by NAME via 'endpointEnv' — never inside this file. Run 'pteam models' ON EACH HOST to list what every role provider actually offers (or 'pteam models --provider <role-provider>' for one, with its thinking options). Route shapes follow the family exactly as in model-routing.example.json: pi = '<pi-provider>/<model-id>' with thinking ∈ off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, claude = a bare model id with thinking ∈ off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultracode. For custom pi models in ~/.pi/agent/models.json, a thinkingLevelMap entry of null means the level is silently clamped by pi — treat it as unsupported. OPTIONAL classes SUPERVISOR_GOVERNANCE (must name a *-supervisor provider: the route a Lead seats its Supervisor from) and LEAD_RECOVERY (must name a *-lead provider: the route a Supervisor recovers a Lead from) may be omitted — the file still validates, preflight warns, and the create_agent gate refuses that flow until the class is configured (pteam routing set <CLASS> ...). Every MCP create_agent by a Lead or Supervisor declares its class in labels["team.model-class"] and must match that class's route exactly (provider family+role, model id, thinking level); an update_agent that changes a seat's model/thinking is held to the route of the seat's own class, and team_fork requires a class too. Not covered: remote-paseo.mjs run and a Lead's direct paseo CLI use (docs/model-routing.md, Known gaps). A class routed to a *-supervisor provider (MONITOR_ECONOMY below) cannot be used to seat a Peer. The create_agent gate reads the routes of the ONE host whose connection.type is "local" (MCP create_agent always lands on the local daemon); 'mac-review' below omits the optional classes to show they are per host.
